title: Repeat one small bar chart per group when groups need comparing.
rule: Draw the same bars in one panel per group, on one scale shared by every panel, with the categories in the same order in each, so the eye compares a bar with the bar in the same place next door. Give each panel a title with its group and its size, give the one bar the title names the red point, or the text’s ink where Rule 14.6 sets ink in its place, with every other bar in light gray, and place as many panels across as fit, one across on a phone.
use_when: The reader asks how the same mix or ranking differs from group to group, such as the evidence grades behind each topic, or there are more groups than four inks can carry (Rule 14.8).

use_instead.when: There are two to four groups and the reader compares them within each category
Each group’s parts add to one whole and the whole is the point
Each group is one value, so a panel would hold one bar

text: Panels that repeat one design let the reader learn the chart once and then read every group the same way. A shared scale keeps a long bar in one panel the same size as a long bar in another, which separate scales would break without any sign on the page.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form small-multiple-bars: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s23, or copy specs/s23.json and point it at a new dataset; encode.panel names the column that splits the panels, labels.point the one bar in red by panel and category, and scale.x the scale they share, from zero to the largest value when it is left out.
caption: How sure is the evidence behind each of the five topic hubs?
